core_obligations: Prove the case n = 1 directly from the three hypotheses on the family of subfields (proof lines 11432-11434).
Assume the result for subspaces of K to the n-1 and let V be a subspace of K to the n meeting every K_alpha to the n nontrivially (proof lines 11435-11437).

If V meets 0 plus k to the n-1 nontrivially there is nothing to prove; otherwise use the induction hypothesis to choose alpha with V cap 0 plus K_alpha to the n-1 equal to zero, and pick a nonzero v in V cap K_alpha to the n, whose first coordinate is then nonzero (proof lines 11437-11444).

Scale v so that its first coordinate is 1; then V cap K_alpha to the n is exactly K_alpha v, and applying the same argument inside a subfield K_alpha' contained in K_alpha shows that the last n-1 coordinates of v lie in every such K_alpha', hence in k, so v lies in V cap k to the n (proof lines 11444-11453).
proof_roadmap: Interval comparison against the public records of more-algebra.tex: no recorded interval covers 11417-11455. The nearest record is 345 (11457-11518, tag 07P4, filtered subfield intersections and characteristic-p differentials), which is the very next statement of the same block and starts two lines after this card's proof ends; it is a different statement, about differentials rather than about subspaces intersecting the base field.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a descent statement for linear algebra over a filtering family of subfields: given a family of subfields K_alpha of K with common intersection k, containing k, and filtering downwards, a subspace V of K to the n has nonzero intersection with k to the n exactly when it has nonzero intersection with K_alpha to the n for every alpha (statement lines 11417-11429). The proof is a 24-line induction on n (proof lines 11432-11455). The induction step is the real content: if some nonzero v lies in V cap K_alpha to the n and the last n-1 coordinates are not enough to win, one first chooses alpha with V cap 0 plus K_alpha to the n-1 equal to zero and then replaces v by a scalar multiple so that its first coordinate is 1, which forces V cap K_alpha to the n to equal K_alpha times v; applying the same argument to a subfield K_alpha' contained in K_alpha shows that the remaining coordinates of v lie in every such K_alpha', hence in k by the intersection and filtering hypotheses, and v itself is then a nonzero element of V cap k to the n.
